The differential equation that generates the slope field shown above is given by
${y}^{′}=(x-a)(y-b).$
Find the value of $a+b.$
feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14045300/assets/e9011b88061abae826e12742ccd47a272bef9e969f204cd7e8ca63edf908a7f8.png)

 

Notice that the slopes of the slope field are horizontal along the lines $x=2$ and $y=2,$ as shown above. Therefore, the right-hand side of the differential equation should evaluate to zero on both of these lines. 

So, our differential equation must be

$$
{y}^{′}=(x-2)(y-2).
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $a=2,$ $b=2,$ and $a+b=4.$
